label: <DEL> delimiter step (subset), strongest for short sequences
explanation: Fires only at the <DEL> delimiter step (t == L, the step that outputs original token 0); never fires during the original or copy phases. It fires on about 64.5% of delimiter steps. Whether it fires and how strongly depends on L: rate falls from about 0.9 of delimiter steps at L<=5 to about 0.3-0.4 at L=7-9, with a slight rebound at L=9. Magnitude is also higher when the first original token (the token output at this step) is 3, c, z, 2, 1, o, l or q; the top activations are mostly short sequences starting with 3. Adding first-token or length conditions only shifts F1 by about a point, so the simple delimiter predicate (recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0, precision ~0.65) is kept. The missing precision comes from delimiter steps in longer sequences and with other first tokens, and no clean rule separates those.
